subject: math
title: Sequence and Series
syllabus: Arithmetic and geometric progressions; insertion of arithmetic and geometric means between two given numbers; relation between A.M. and G.M.; sum of n terms of special series (Σn, Σn², Σn³); telescoping sums.

body:
Each term adds the same d:
a_{n} = a + (n − 1)d, S_{n} = \f{n}{2}[2a + (n − 1)d] = \f{n}{2}(a + l)
Gauss's trick: write the sum forwards and backwards — every pair adds to (first + last).
Terms equally far from the ends add up the same: a_{1} + a_{n} = a_{2} + a_{n−1} = …
a_{n} = S_{n} − S_{n−1}. If S_{n} = pn^{2} + qn then d = 2p.
Choose terms smartly: three in A.P. → a − d, a, a + d; four → a − 3d, a − d, a + d, a + 3d (difference 2d).
Even number of terms 2k: (sum of even-placed) − (sum of odd-placed) = kd.

Each term multiplies by r:
a_{n} = ar^{n−1}, S_{n} = a\f{r^{n} − 1}{r − 1} (r ≠ 1), S_{∞} = \f{a}{1 − r} (|r| < 1)
Terms equally far from the ends MULTIPLY to the same: a_{3}a_{5} = a_{4}^{2}, a_{1}a_{5} = a_{3}^{2}.
Three in G.P.: \f{a}{r}, a, ar (product a^{3}). Dividing two terms kills a: \f{a_{m}}{a_{n}} = r^{m−n}.
If a_{1}, a_{2}, … is a G.P. then a_{1}^{3}, a_{2}^{3}, … is a G.P. with ratio r^{3}.

body: b is the A.M. of a, c if 2b = a + c; the G.M. if b^{2} = ac.
n arithmetic means between a and b: d = \f{b − a}{n + 1}; their sum is n × \f{a + b}{2}.
For positive numbers: A.M. ≥ G.M. (equality only when all are equal)
So y + \f{1}{y} ≥ 2 for y > 0 — the key to many "least value" questions.
Mixed problems: write the A.P. condition and the G.P. condition as two equations and solve.
Telescoping: write each term as f(k) − f(k + 1); everything in the middle cancels.
The JEE favourite: 1 + 4k^{4} = (2k^{2} + 1)^{2} − (2k)^{2} = (2k^{2} − 2k + 1)(2k^{2} + 2k + 1); the two factors differ by 4k.

traps: S_{n} = 0 does not mean any term is 0.
"Increasing G.P. of positive terms" decides between r and 1/r.
A.M. ≥ G.M. only for POSITIVE numbers.
For four terms in A.P. written a − 3d, …, a + 3d the common difference is 2d.
Count terms carefully: rows of a triangle use 1 + 2 + … + k terms.

An arithmetic progression is written in the following way: row 1: 2; row 2: 5, 8; row 3: 11, 14, 17; row 4: 20, 23, 26, 29; … The sum of all the terms of the 10^{th} row is ______
sol: Row k has k terms, so rows 1–9 use 45 terms; row 10 is terms 46 to 55 of 2, 5, 8, … (d = 3).

pyq.q: Let A be the set of first 101 terms of an A.P., whose first term is 1 and the common difference is 5 and let B be the set of first 71 terms of an A.P., whose first term is 9 and the common difference is 7. Then the number of elements in A ∩ B, which are divisible by 3, is :
sol: Common terms: x ≡ 1 (mod 5), x ≡ 2 (mod 7) → 16, 51, 86, …, 471 (14 terms, up to min(501, 499)).
Divisible by 3 as well: 16 + 35t with t ≡ 1 (mod 3) → t = 1, 4, 7, 10, 13 → 5 numbers.
